edges.description: Different alleles may perturb splicing, binding partners, ubiquitin handling, or other UBA1-dependent processes through mechanisms not yet established in patient tissue.
Human anterior-horn pathology is established, but the intervening allele-specific UBA1 mechanism is unknown.
Human sensory involvement forms a separate branch from anterior-horn motor-neuron degeneration; its UBA1-dependent route is unknown.
Cerebellar pathology was observed in one detailed human autopsy, but its relationship to specific UBA1 alleles is unresolved.
Muscle-targeted knockdown supports a parallel model-only tissue-autonomous branch whose fidelity to human SMAX2 remains untested.
Motor neuron loss denervates skeletal muscle, producing congenital hypotonia, areflexia, and profound weakness.
In utero motor-system dysfunction can reduce fetal movement and thereby promote congenital joint contractures.
intermediate_mechanisms: Reduced fetal movement and prolonged joint immobility

edges.description: The human neurophysiologic and postmortem sensory findings manifest clinically as sensory nervous system involvement.
The observed cerebellar pathology is represented by the corresponding structural phenotype.
Congenital lower-motor-unit dysfunction manifests as neonatal hypotonia.
Lower-motor-unit dysfunction produces absent deep-tendon reflexes.
Denervation and possible muscle-autonomous dysfunction produce generalized or distal weakness across the clinical spectrum.
Facial muscle weakness produces the characteristic myopathic facial appearance.
Phrenic and intercostal motor unit failure compromises ventilation.
Bulbar and generalized weakness impair sucking and swallowing.
Progressive neuromuscular weakness can produce secondary spinal curvature.
intermediate_mechanisms: Chronic axial weakness and asymmetric loading during growth.

edges.description: Prenatal motor-system dysfunction manifests as reduced fetal movement.
Fetal akinesia from motor neuron loss produces multiple congenital joint contractures.
Fractures co-occur with congenital contractures, but the direct causal substrate is unknown.
Muscle-intrinsic UBA1 reduction may contribute to weakness alongside denervation.

nodes.description: SMAX2-associated hemizygous variants cluster in exon 15 near the active adenylation domain, but they do not share one demonstrated biochemical defect. The recurrent synonymous c.1731C>T allele reduces UBA1 expression. In vitro, p.Met539Ile and p.Ser547Gly did not show statistically reduced adenylation, whereas p.Glu557Val showed a moderate reduction. The initiating lesion is therefore modeled as allele-specific UBA1 dysfunction rather than uniform adenylation failure or complete loss of UBA1 function.

nodes.description: UBA1 is the initiating enzyme of the ubiquitin cascade, but human SMAX2 tissue has not shown a uniform decrease in ubiquitination or proteasomal degradation. Variant biochemistry instead points to allele-specific effects and possible non-catalytic mechanisms such as altered splicing or binding partners. This node keeps those candidate cellular routes explicit without projecting the decreased ubiquitination seen after experimental knockdown onto human pathology.
